question: Backlog B46: the square torus's law-(12, 12) automaton reads its distance plainly only when grouped into rings of linear size (REROUTE-20261109-001B, Theorem 3), as its two line networks are. Can its cells be grouped into long rings running in two directions, on time with ring balls growing like a plane's? Among the periodic groupings, which are on time, and what do their rings and ring graphs look like?

public_inputs.run: run.py in this folder, 6 worker processes.
public_inputs.family: Every grouping of the n x n square torus invariant under a sublattice <(a, 0), (b, c)> (Hermite normal form) of index ac at most 8 containing n Z^2, for n = 24 and 16, and of index at most 6 for n = 12: each re-routes H(p) and V(p) by p mod the sublattice, 4^(ac) patterns per lattice.
public_inputs.readings: Whether the pattern is a network; the plain first need of every ring at every target of one fundamental domain, exact (shortest-route parities); for on-time groupings, every ring's homology class, the number of rings and their sizes, and the ring graph's balls of radius 0 to 10 from one ring.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the roster or the hypotheses after seeing results
primary_observable: The on-time groupings, with their rings' homology classes up to sign (H1) and whether their ring graph is a cycle (H2).
cheapest_meaningful_control: The two line networks (re-routed at every horizontal or every vertical contact) are periodic under the full lattice (index 1) and on time (REROUTE-20261109-001B, Theorem 2).
decision_or_followup_rule: Frozen hypotheses. H1: every on-time grouping read is a family of parallel lines: every ring non-contractible and all of one homology class up to sign. H2: every on-time grouping read has a ring graph that is a cycle (balls of 2r + 1 rings until all are reached). If both hold, the periodic groupings give no plane of long rings: what reads plainly is a family of lines, of several slopes. If H1 fails with an on-time grouping of crossing rings, its ring graph and balls are read; growth faster than linear would be a plane of long rings.
stop_rule: Stop when every pattern of the roster has its readings.
nonclaims: Exploratory and finite: periodic groupings with period cells of at most 8 contacts' worth only; non-periodic groupings are not read.
Law (12, 12) on the square torus only; two-time knots only (A30).
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing, a pilot (scratch, not kept) read the groupings periodic under rectangular sublattices a x b with ab at most 6 on the 12 x 12 torus (1,014 networks, 28 on time, all of them the two line networks), and under the sublattices <(a, 0), (b, c)> with 0 <= b < c of index at most 6 on the 24 x 24 torus (3,157 networks, 68 on time: the axis line networks, 54 times, and families of 24 rings of 96 contacts in the classes (1, 1) and (1, -1) and of 16 rings of 144 in the classes (2, 1) and (1, 2), every one with a cyclic ring graph). That pilot's parametrisation skipped the lattices with b >= c and repeated others; this census uses the Hermite normal form 0 <= b < a, so most lattices of index 4 to 8 are read here for the first time. H1 and H2 were written from the pilot.
